subject: Repeated measures / widget to select from a user-defined list

messages.author: 1a09129d38549286
messages.subject: Repeated measures / widget to select from a user-defined list
parts:
Hello,

Experiments of repeated measures are very frequent in my work, so I
think it would be nice to have a dialog to analyse them in Deducer,
just as there are dialogs for other kinds of linear models. This leads
to my first question: is there any planned development of such a
dialog in future versios of Deducer?

If the answer is "no" (or "yes, but we accept some collaboration"), I
would be willing to contribute to it. I have sketched (but still not
programmed) a conceptual, simplified draft of how that dialog could be
designed and the R code to run, inspired in the extant dialog for
linear models. However, although I have managed to build very simple
Deducer dialogs, following the instructions of Deducer's wiki
("Development" section), my knowledge of rJava is virtually
inexistent, so I cannot write the code of such an sketch.

My main obstacle is the specification of the between- and within-
subject models, by means of some kind of selector widgets. (Of course
it would be always possible to ask the user type the formulae, as
Rcommander does, but that's not the style of Deducer, I think.) So
here comes my second question: is there an "easy way" of creating a
widget like the VariableSelectorWidget (and VariableListWidget/
SingleVariableWidget pointing to it), that do not show the list of
variables in the selected data frame, but a user-defined list of
items? E.g., the selected factors of the model, to specify the main
and interaction effects, or the least square means in sub-menus.

Thanks in advance
Helios

parts:
Helios,

I most definitely welcome collaborations. You are absolutely right to
draw out on paper the dialog design, and to spec out the r code
required.

regarding your second question... If I understand right, you want
something like the list example in DeducerPlugInExample, which goes
something like:

leftList <- new(ListWidget,"Left hand list",c("Item 1","Item 2","Item
3","Item 4"))
setSize(leftList,150,210)
rightList <- new(ListWidget,"Right hand list")
setSize(rightList,150,210)
buttons <- new(AddRemoveButtons,leftList,rightList)

dialog <- new(SimpleRDialog)
dialog$setSize(500L,300L)
addComponent(dialog,leftList,10,400,600,450,,,"NONE","NONE")
addComponent(dialog,rightList,10,900,600,450,,,"NONE","NONE")
addComponent(dialog,buttons,100,600,600,450,"NONE","NONE")

Ian

messages.subject: Re: Repeated measures / widget to select from a user-defined list
parts:
Hi, Helios,

I've got the beginnings of an interface for ezANOVA (in package 'ez')
that you might take a look at. It permits the specification of
between and within-subjects factors (as well as "observed" factors).
The plotting only does 1 or 2 factors at a time at the moment, and the
Tukey post-hoc tests only work on between-subjects factors. I'm
working on a way to do simple main effects testing that should work
for between-subjects and within-subjects factors. The interface also
allows you to convert wide-form data (1 subject per row) to long-form
data (1 row per within-subjects-factor response). I'd be happy to
hear any suggestions you have.

Unfortunately, the Windows binary build isn't cooperating at the
moment but you can take a look at all the source code here:

https://r-forge.r-project.org/scm/viewvc.php/pkg/DeducerANOVA/R/?root=richoutput

--Bill

messages.author: 1a09129d38549286
messages.subject: Re: Repeated measures / widget to select from a user-defined list
parts:
Hi, Bill,

I'd be pleased to collaborate in your project; it would of course be
more efficient than duplicating efforts for similar ideas.

I had planned to use lm plus Anova from package 'car', plus a custom-
made wrapper to lht (linearHypotesis) to perform post-hoc paired (or
more complex) comparisons for main effects, as well as simple effects
or interaction contrasts. Since as far as I know, ezANOVA is based on
Anova, it wouldn't make a lot of difference, but I prefer the
flexibility of Anova to cope with customized models.

ezANOVA avoids the trouble of defining the between- and within-factor
formulas, but at the cost of only analysing full factorial models (as
far as I have managed to explore). For instance, if you analyse the
OBrienKaiser dataset (two between-subject factors --gender and
treatment--, plus two within-subject factors --phase and hour--),
ezANOVA lets me analyze a model whose formula would be
gender*treatment*phase*hour, but I have not been able to analyze
simpler models, for instance without higher order interactions --which
may be convenient in many cases.

I think that using Anova and allowing the user to customize the model
would be more inline with Deducer's tool for Linear Models. Anyway,
I'm open to discussion in this point. I'll contact you privately to
continue on commenting on this.

Helios
